# Tax prep notes

Checklist for the freelance side of the household return.

## Documents to gather

W-2s from employers, 1099-NEC and 1099-K for freelance and platform income, 1099-INT and 1099-DIV for interest, 1098 for mortgage interest, 1095-A if we had marketplace coverage, and receipts for charitable gifts. Last year's return is useful for comparison.

## Estimated tax payments

Freelance income has no tax withheld, so we send estimated tax four times a year: April 15, June 15, September 15 and January 15. To avoid an underpayment penalty, pay at least 90% of this year's tax or 100% of last year's tax (110% if adjusted gross income was over $150,000).

## Home office deduction

The space must be used regularly and exclusively for work. The simplified method is $5 per square foot, up to 300 square feet, for a maximum deduction of $1,500. The regular method uses the actual share of rent, utilities and insurance, and takes more paperwork.

## Mileage and car

Business miles are deductible at the IRS standard rate per mile, with a log showing the date, destination and purpose of each trip. Commuting to a regular workplace does not count.

## Keeping records

Keep tax returns and the receipts behind them for at least 3 years from the date you file. Keep them 6 years if you left out more than 25% of your income, and indefinitely if you never filed. Records for a house or investments are kept until 3 years after you sell.

## Charitable donations

A written acknowledgment is needed for any single gift of $250 or more. For donated goods, keep a list and the thrift store's receipt.
